Holds for any account key and for a Monzo re-import with or without --opening-balance (sha is of the raw bytes). Proven by test_p9_importing_a_file_twice_leaves_the_same_state_and_log_head_as_once[csv,monzo] and test_p9_holds_for_generated_statements[3 archetypes], PASSED in invariants-5.log:211-215 and specified-3.log:325-333.

store.py:601-606 calls _same_account (store.py:624-655) inside _recorded before any input/statement write; it reloads each imported account's statements/<account>.csv, intersects (date, signed pence) multisets over the overlapping period and refuses when more than half the new statement's overlap lines are shared, saying 'probably the same account imported twice'. Opposite-sign own-account transfers and non-overlapping periods are not matched. A refusal raises inside _recorded, so undo runs and nothing is appended. Proven by test_an_account_sharing_most_date_amount_pairs_with_an_overlapping_one_is_refused and test_an_account_that_is_not_the_same_one_is_added[body0-2], PASSED in contracts-4.log:76-79. Only caller is cli.py:572.

Tests assert every file's bytes in the case folder and the verified log head are unchanged after a second import under 'main' and another key, through the library and the CLI, for csv, monzo and three generated statements; marked invariants with p9 in the name, and the runner's invariants tier ran them (invariants-5.log:211-215).

findings.claim: _same_account fails open. It skips any existing account whose statements/<account>.csv cannot be read or loaded, and it never compares the file with the statement_sha256 its import entry records. So if a statement file is damaged or replaced, a duplicate of that account is admitted. The producer reported this gap themselves. Other case damage, such as a hand-edited log, is outside scope elsewhere, so this is minor.
findings.repro: Import a.csv as main. Overwrite <case>/statements/main.csv with 'garbage'. Import a copy of a.csv's lines under new ids as --account s. The import is added instead of refused.

findings.claim: The test for 'most' uses only the new statement's lines inside the overlapping period, so a single coincident line is enough to refuse a separate account. Nothing (no override or flag) lets the underwriter add a genuinely separate account that this rule refuses. This meets R40's literal wording (1 of 1 is most) but is not stated in the design.
findings.repro: main covers 2026-01-01..2026-01-31 with a -15.00 fee on 2026-01-31. savings covers 2026-01-31..2026-03-31, and its 2026-01-31 line is also -15.00. Importing savings is refused as 'probably the same account imported twice'.
